trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Lisbon, Portugal
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

experiences.name: Time Out Market Lisbon Food Tour
experiences.description: Explore Portugal's premier food hall featuring the best local chefs and traditional dishes under one roof. Sample pastéis de nata, prego sandwiches, grilled sardines, and regional cheeses while mingling with locals in a vibrant market atmosphere.

experiences.name: São Jorge Castle & Mouraria Neighborhood Walk
experiences.description: Explore the Moorish-era São Jorge Castle perched atop Lisbon's highest hill, offering panoramic city views and archaeological ruins dating back 3,000 years. Descend into the multicultural Mouraria quarter, the birthplace of Fado, and discover hidden tascas serving petiscos (Portuguese tapas).

day_by_day.morning: Arrival — Flight TP lands at 13:00, so no morning activities. Take the Aerobus (Line 1, ~€4) or Metro Vermelha (Red Line, ~€1.65) from Humberto Delgado Airport to central Lisbon. Check in at Lisbon City Stay and freshen up.
day_by_day.afternoon: After settling in, take a gentle orientation walk through Baixa (Downtown Lisbon). Stroll along Rua Augusta pedestrian street, admire the Arco da Rua Augusta (free exterior view), and head down to Praça do Comércio on the Tagus riverfront — all free to enjoy. Get your bearings and soak in the city atmosphere.
day_by_day.evening: Head to the Time Out Market Lisbon for your first taste of authentic Portuguese food. Browse stalls from top local chefs at accessible prices (dishes typically €5–€12 each). Try a bifana sandwich, fresh seafood, or a classic pastry. The market is lively and perfect for solo or group budget dining without committing to a full restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Grab a coffee and pastel de nata at the airport or a café near the hotel upon arrival (~€2–€3)
meals.lunch: Skip or grab a quick bifana sandwich from a local snack bar near Baixa (~€3–€4)
meals.dinner: Time Out Market Lisbon — budget €10–€15 for a satisfying meal with a drink. Share a few small plates to sample more dishes.

day_by_day.notes: Validate your Metro/bus card (Viva Viagem card, €0.50) at the airport — it saves money over single tickets. The Tagus riverfront walk from Praça do Comércio is completely free and stunning at sunset. Keep energy light today after travel.

day_by_day.morning: Start the day with the São Jorge Castle & Mouraria Neighborhood Walk. Arrive at São Jorge Castle early (opens 9:00) to beat crowds — admission is ~€15 but offers panoramic views over all of Lisbon. Walk the ramparts and explore the archaeological site inside. Afterward, descend into the historic Mouraria neighborhood, Lisbon's oldest and most multicultural district, and wander its winding alleyways for free.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Alfama district on foot — Lisbon's oldest neighborhood. Visit the Miradouro da Graça or Miradouro de Santa Luzia (free viewpoints) for stunning city and river views. Browse the local market stalls if any are open, and pop into the Se Cathedral (Lisbon Cathedral) — free exterior, small fee ~€3 for cloisters. Walk downhill through Alfama's narrow lanes.
day_by_day.evening: Experience authentic Fado music — the soul of Lisbon. Head to a tasca (local tavern) in Alfama or Mouraria that offers free Fado with dinner. Restaurants like Mesa de Frades or smaller local tascas often have live Fado. Alternatively, enjoy a budget dinner at a local tasca and listen to street Fado performers in Alfama for free.

meals.breakfast: Café near the hotel — galão (milky coffee) and a tosta mista (toasted sandwich) for ~€3–€4
meals.lunch: Local tasca in Mouraria — prato do dia (daily special) typically includes soup, main, bread, and a drink for €7–€10
meals.dinner: Alfama tasca dinner with Fado atmosphere — bacalhau (salt cod) dish or caldo verde soup + main for €12–€16 total

day_by_day.notes: Wear comfortable shoes — Alfama and Mouraria are hilly with cobblestone streets. The 28E tram is iconic but very crowded and pickpocket-prone on weekends; consider walking or taking Bus 737 instead. São Jorge Castle is the priciest entry this trip — check if your accommodation offers discount vouchers.

day_by_day.morning: Take Bus 714 or Tram 15E (~€1.65) out to Belém for the Belém Historic Monuments & Pastry Walk. Start at the iconic Tower of Belém (Torre de Belém, ~€6 entry) on the Tagus riverfront, a stunning 16th-century fortified tower. Walk along the riverside promenade — the views are spectacular and free.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the UNESCO-listed Jerónimos Monastery (Mosteiro dos Jerónimos, ~€10 entry or free on Sundays before 14:00 — check current policy). This is one of Portugal's greatest architectural masterpieces in Manueline style. Afterward, visit the Monument to the Discoveries (Padrão dos Descobrimentos, ~€6) or admire it from outside for free. Explore the surrounding Belém gardens at no cost.
day_by_day.evening: Return to central Lisbon. Explore the Chiado and Bairro Alto neighborhoods in the early evening — window shop, browse independent bookshops like Livraria Bertrand (world's oldest bookshop, free to enter), and enjoy the bohemian atmosphere. Bairro Alto comes alive in the evening with budget-friendly bars and tascas.

meals.breakfast: Stop at the legendary Pastéis de Belém bakery (the original since 1837) for 2–3 pastéis de nata fresh from the oven with cinnamon and sugar — ~€2.50 total. A bucket-list Lisbon experience.
meals.lunch: Picnic-style lunch from a local Belém supermarket or grab a prego (steak sandwich) from a nearby café for €4–€6
meals.dinner: Bairro Alto budget tasca — try carne de porco à alentejana (pork with clams) or grilled sardines for €10–€14 including a glass of house wine

day_by_day.notes: Sunday mornings are ideal for Jerónimos Monastery — free entry before 14:00 (verify this policy closer to your travel date). Belém is about 6km from central Lisbon; Tram 15E is the most scenic route. Bring a light jacket as the riverside can be breezy.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the historic Príncipe Real neighborhood — one of Lisbon's most charming and elegant quarters. Visit the Jardim do Príncipe Real (free garden with a beautiful 19th-century cedar tree), browse the Monday antique and organic market (if running), and admire the grand 19th-century mansions. Walk to the nearby Miradouro de São Pedro de Alcântara for sweeping views over the city — completely free.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the National Museum of Ancient Art (Museu Nacional de Arte Antiga, ~€6 entry) — Portugal's most important art museum housing Hieronymus Bosch's Temptations of St. Anthony and significant Portuguese historical artifacts. Alternatively, explore the Carmo Convent (Convento do Carmo, ~€5) in Chiado — a hauntingly beautiful roofless Gothic ruin turned archaeological museum, destroyed in the 1755 earthquake.
day_by_day.evening: Join or self-guide a walk through Intendente and Mouraria for a deeper dive into multicultural Lisbon history. End the evening at a local cervejaria (beer hall) or a tasca in Intendente — one of Lisbon's most authentic and budget-friendly dining neighborhoods, less touristy than Alfama.

meals.breakfast: Padaria (local bakery) near the hotel — fresh bread roll with butter and coffee for €2–€3
meals.lunch: Príncipe Real area — try a simple restaurant offering the menú do dia (set lunch menu) for €8–€10 including starter, main, dessert or coffee
meals.dinner: Intendente neighborhood tasca — honest Portuguese home cooking, expect to pay €10–€13 for a hearty dinner with house wine or local beer

day_by_day.notes: Monday can mean some museums are closed — double-check opening days before visiting. The Carmo Convent is a particularly moving historical site given its earthquake history and is very budget-friendly. Príncipe Real market typically runs on Saturdays but check local listings for Monday options.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Feira da Ladra flea market at Campo de Santa Clara (runs Tuesdays and Saturdays, free entry). This centuries-old market is a treasure trove of vintage items, antiques, old books, and Portuguese curiosities — great for budget souvenirs. Browse the stalls and practice your bargaining. The nearby Igreja de São Vicente de Fora church (~€5) offers rooftop views and stunning azulejo tile panels.
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend the afternoon at the National Tile Museum (Museu Nacional do Azulejo, ~€5 entry) — a must for history lovers. Housed in a stunning 16th-century convent, it traces 500 years of Portuguese azulejo (decorative tile) art, including a remarkable 23-meter panoramic tile panel of pre-earthquake Lisbon from 1738. This is one of Lisbon's most unique and underrated museums.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the Time Out Market Lisbon for a final celebratory meal — this time try dishes you haven't yet tasted, such as fresh grilled fish, petiscos (Portuguese tapas), or a local dessert like arroz doce (rice pudding). Toast your trip with a glass of ginjinha (sour cherry liqueur, ~€1.50) from a street kiosk near Rossio Square — a beloved Lisbon tradition.

meals.breakfast: Rossio Square area café — pastel de nata and espresso (bica) for €2.50, a perfect final morning ritual
meals.lunch: Grab street food or a quick snack at the Feira da Ladra market area — grilled chouriço, sandwiches, or local pastries for €4–€6
meals.dinner: Time Out Market Lisbon farewell meal — budget €12–€18 for a generous final spread with a local craft beer or glass of Vinho Verde

day_by_day.notes: The National Tile Museum is a short bus or taxi ride from the center (~€1.65 by bus). Buy ginjinha in a chocolate cup near Rossio for the full experience (~€2). Pack your bags tonight if departing tomorrow. Keep receipts for any VAT refund claims on purchases over €50. Lisbon has been wonderful — obrigado!

trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Lisbon Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Clear immigration, collect luggage, and take the Aerobus or Metro (Red Line to Green Line) to central Lisbon. Check in to Lisbon City Stay and freshen up.
day_by_day.afternoon: Settle in and take a relaxed self-guided walk through Baixa (Downtown Lisbon) and Chiado. Stroll along Rua Augusta, cross Praça do Comércio by the Tagus River, and ride the historic Elevador de Santa Justa for panoramic rooftop views of the city (€5.30). A gentle introduction to Lisbon's architecture and street life.
day_by_day.evening: Alfama Fado & Dinner Experience — head to Alfama, Lisbon's oldest and most atmospheric neighborhood, for an authentic Fado music dinner. Enjoy traditional Portuguese dishes (bacalhau, caldo verde) paired with soulful, UNESCO-recognized Fado performances in an intimate tasca setting.

meals.breakfast: Grab a pastel de nata and espresso (bica) at a café near the airport or upon arrival in the city center — try Pastelaria Versailles near Avenida.
meals.lunch: Light snack or sandwich at a café in Baixa after check-in, such as A Cevicheria Snack Bar or a local pastelaria (~€8–12).
meals.dinner: Included as part of the Alfama Fado & Dinner Experience — traditional Portuguese dinner with wine and live Fado (~€40–55 per person).

day_by_day.notes: Day 1 is intentionally light given the 13:00 arrival. Pre-book the Fado dinner experience in advance as spots fill quickly, especially on weekends. The Metro from the airport to Baixa-Chiado takes about 25 minutes and costs ~€1.65 with a Viva Viagem card.

day_by_day.morning: LX Factory Sunday Market & Local Brunch — Sunday is the perfect day to visit LX Factory, a repurposed 19th-century industrial complex in Alcântara. Browse stalls selling vintage goods, local crafts, books, and artisan products. Enjoy a leisurely brunch at one of the eclectic restaurants or cafés inside the complex.
day_by_day.afternoon: Belém Historic Monuments & Pastry Walk — just a short walk or tram ride from LX Factory, explore UNESCO-listed Jerónimos Monastery (€10), a stunning example of Manueline architecture, and the iconic Tower of Belém (€6). Walk along the riverside promenade and soak in the maritime history of Portugal's Age of Discovery.
day_by_day.evening: Return to central Lisbon and explore the Príncipe Real neighborhood — a charming, upscale residential area with tree-lined squares, antique shops, and excellent restaurants. Enjoy a relaxed Sunday evening dinner at a local restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Brunch at LX Factory — try the popular brunch spots inside like O Corvo or a market stall offering açaí bowls, eggs, and local pastries (~€12–18).
meals.lunch: Stop at the legendary Pastéis de Belém bakery (the original since 1837) for freshly baked pastéis de nata with cinnamon and powdered sugar (~€1.50 each). Pair with a coffee for a classic Lisbon afternoon treat.
meals.dinner: Dinner in Príncipe Real — try Taberna da Rua das Flores for traditional Portuguese petiscos (small plates) in a cozy tavern setting (~€25–35 per person).

day_by_day.notes: LX Factory is busiest on Sundays — arrive by 11:00 to avoid crowds. Belém is about 6 km west of the city center; take Tram 15E from Praça da Figueira or an Uber (~€8). Jerónimos Monastery is free on Sundays until 14:00 for EU citizens — check current policy before visiting.

day_by_day.morning: São Jorge Castle & Mouraria Neighborhood Walk — begin the morning at São Jorge Castle (€15), the Moorish-era fortress perched atop Lisbon's highest hill offering sweeping panoramic views over the city and the Tagus River. Explore the ramparts, towers, and archaeological ruins at your own pace.
day_by_day.afternoon: Descend from the castle into Mouraria, Lisbon's historic Moorish quarter and the birthplace of Fado. Wander through narrow cobblestone lanes, discover street art, and visit Intendente Square. Continue to the vibrant Martim Moniz Square and explore the multicultural food stalls and market.
day_by_day.evening: Visit the National Tile Museum (Museu Nacional do Azulejo) — a short Uber or bus ride away (~€5). Marvel at Portugal's iconic azulejo tile art spanning five centuries, including a stunning 23-meter panoramic tile panel of pre-earthquake Lisbon. End the evening with dinner in the Alfama or Graça area.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at a local café near the hotel — try A Padaria Portuguesa chain for fresh bread, croissants, and coffee (~€5–8).
meals.lunch: Lunch at a tasca in Mouraria — look for the daily lunch special (prato do dia) which typically includes soup, main course, bread, and a drink for €9–13. Try Zé da Mouraria for authentic local cuisine.
meals.dinner: Dinner in Graça neighborhood — try Chapitô à Mesa for Portuguese cuisine with a stunning terrace view over the city (~€25–35 per person).

day_by_day.notes: Arrive at São Jorge Castle early (opens at 09:00) to beat tour groups. The National Tile Museum is closed on Mondays — if so, replace the evening activity with a walk through the Graça viewpoint (Miradouro da Graça) and explore the area's local bars and wine shops instead.

day_by_day.morning: Time Out Market Lisbon Food Tour — spend the morning at the iconic Time Out Market in Cais do Sodré, Portugal's premier food hall featuring top local chefs and traditional dishes under one roof. This is an ideal way to sample a wide variety of Portuguese cuisine including fresh seafood, charcuterie, bifanas, and ginjinha.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Cais do Sodré and Santos neighborhoods on foot. Visit the colorful Pink Street (Rua Nova do Carvalho) and browse independent boutiques and galleries in Santos. Head to the Museum of Art, Architecture and Technology (MAAT) along the riverfront for contemporary art and architecture (€5–9) — a beautiful building with a rooftop walkway over the Tagus.
day_by_day.evening: Take a scenic sunset boat cruise on the Tagus River — 1.5 to 2-hour cruises depart from Cais do Sodré and offer views of the 25 de Abril Bridge, Cristo Rei statue, and the Lisbon skyline at golden hour (~€25–35 per person). End the evening with a nightcap in the Bairro Alto neighborhood.

meals.breakfast: Coffee and pastry at Café de São Bento or a neighborhood café near the hotel (~€5–7).
meals.lunch: Full food tour experience at Time Out Market — budget €20–30 per person to sample multiple stalls including seafood, petiscos, and dessert. Don't miss the grilled octopus and pastéis de bacalhau.
meals.dinner: Casual dinner at a tasca in Bairro Alto after the boat cruise — try Tasca do Chico or Zé da Mouraria for hearty Portuguese comfort food (~€20–28 per person).

day_by_day.notes: Time Out Market opens at 10:00 — arriving early on a weekday means shorter queues at popular stalls. Book the Tagus sunset cruise in advance online, especially in May when days are longer and demand is high. The MAAT museum has free entry on the last Sunday of each month.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the National Museum of Ancient Art (Museu Nacional de Arte Antiga) — Portugal's most important art museum, housing masterpieces including Hieronymus Bosch's 'Temptations of St. Anthony' and an extraordinary collection of Portuguese gold and silverwork, azulejos, and colonial-era artifacts (€6). Located in a 17th-century palace near Santos.
day_by_day.afternoon: Final afternoon stroll through Chiado and Bairro Alto — browse the iconic Livraria Bertrand (world's oldest operating bookshop, est. 1732), explore independent boutiques, and stop at Miradouro de Santa Catarina for a relaxed viewpoint experience with local street musicians. Pick up souvenirs such as local wine, ginjinha, canned sardines, and cork products.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner at a special restaurant in Chiado or Bairro Alto — splurge slightly for the final night at a well-regarded Portuguese restaurant. Enjoy a multi-course meal with regional wines, finishing with a glass of Port wine and pastel de nata for dessert.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely breakfast at Café A Brasileira in Chiado — one of Lisbon's most historic cafés, famous for its Art Deco interior and the bronze statue of poet Fernando Pessoa outside (~€8–12).
meals.lunch: Light lunch at a tasca or wine bar in Santos or Chiado — try a francesinha (Porto-style sandwich) or a plate of presunto and queijo with local wine (~€15–20).
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at Alma Restaurant in Chiado (Chef Henrique Sá Pessoa) or Taberna da Rua das Flores for an elevated but accessible Portuguese dining experience (~€40–60 per person with wine). Reserve in advance.

day_by_day.notes: If departing on Day 6, confirm check-out time with Lisbon City Stay and arrange luggage storage if needed for a late flight. The National Museum of Ancient Art is closed on Mondays and Tuesdays — if visiting on those days, substitute with the Calouste Gulbenkian Museum (one of Europe's finest private collections). Keep Metro or Uber apps handy for efficient movement across the city.

day_by_day.afternoon: Leisurely orientation stroll through the elegant Chiado and Bairro Alto neighborhoods near the hotel. Explore the iconic Praça do Comércio waterfront square and the grand Rua Augusta Arch. Stop into the historic Livraria Bertrand — the world's oldest operating bookshop — for a cultural first impression of Lisbon.
day_by_day.evening: Alfama Fado & Dinner Experience: Head to Lisbon's oldest and most atmospheric neighborhood, Alfama, for an authentic Fado dinner show. Enjoy a curated multi-course Portuguese dinner paired with soulful, UNESCO-recognized Fado music performed by local artists in an intimate traditional venue.

meals.breakfast: Not applicable (in-flight or airport upon arrival)
meals.lunch: Light welcome lunch at the hotel or a nearby upscale café such as Café A Brasileira in Chiado — try a bifana sandwich and a glass of Vinho Verde to kick off the Portuguese culinary experience.
meals.dinner: Included as part of the Alfama Fado & Dinner Experience — expect traditional dishes such as bacalhau à brás, caldo verde soup, and pastel de nata for dessert, paired with Alentejo wines.

day_by_day.notes: Arrival day — keep the schedule relaxed. Book the Fado experience in advance as top venues sell out quickly. Private airport transfer is strongly recommended for a seamless luxury arrival. Tip: pack light layers as Lisbon evenings in May can be breezy.

day_by_day.morning: São Jorge Castle & Mouraria Neighborhood Walk: Begin the day with a guided private tour of the Moorish-era São Jorge Castle perched atop Lisbon's highest hill. Enjoy panoramic views over the city's terracotta rooftops and the Tagus River. Descend into the vibrant Mouraria quarter — Lisbon's multicultural heart — and discover its layered history from Moorish occupation to modern-day life.
day_by_day.afternoon: Time Out Market Lisbon Food Tour: Make your way to the celebrated Time Out Market in Cais do Sodré for an expertly guided food tour. Sample dishes from Portugal's top chefs and producers — from fresh seafood and artisan cheeses to traditional petiscos (Portuguese tapas) and regional wines — all under one iconic roof.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset drinks at a rooftop bar such as Park Bar (Bairro Alto) or TOPO Chiado, offering sweeping views of the city bathed in golden light. Follow with a refined dinner at a Michelin-recognized restaurant in Chiado or Príncipe Real.

meals.breakfast: Indulgent breakfast at the hotel — opt for the full Portuguese spread with fresh pastries, local cheeses, presunto ham, and freshly squeezed orange juice.
meals.lunch: Covered within the Time Out Market Food Tour — a progressive tasting experience across multiple stalls and chef counters.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Belcanto (two Michelin stars, Chef José Avillez) in Chiado — book well in advance. Expect avant-garde Portuguese cuisine celebrating local ingredients with extraordinary creativity.

day_by_day.notes: Saturday is a lively day at Time Out Market — arrive slightly early for the food tour to avoid peak crowds. Belcanto reservations should be made weeks ahead. Comfortable walking shoes are essential for the castle's cobblestone paths.

day_by_day.morning: LX Factory Sunday Market & Local Brunch: Spend a vibrant Sunday morning at LX Factory, a beautifully repurposed 19th-century industrial complex in Alcântara. Browse the weekly market featuring independent designers, vintage finds, artisan food producers, and local crafts. Soak in the creative, bohemian atmosphere unique to Lisbon's cultural scene.
day_by_day.afternoon: Belém Historic Monuments & Pastry Walk: Take a short ride to the UNESCO World Heritage district of Belém. Visit the breathtaking Jerónimos Monastery, a masterpiece of Manueline Gothic architecture, and the iconic Tower of Belém standing sentinel on the Tagus riverbank. Stroll along the waterfront and visit the Monument to the Discoveries. End with the unmissable ritual of tasting a freshly baked pastel de Belém at the legendary Pastéis de Belém bakery, open since 1837.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the city center for a relaxed evening in Príncipe Real — Lisbon's most refined and leafy neighborhood. Browse its antique shops and boutiques before settling in for a long, leisurely dinner.

meals.breakfast: Brunch at LX Factory — try the popular Landeau Chocolate café for their famous chocolate cake, or enjoy a full brunch spread at one of the market's artisan food stalls.
meals.lunch: Riverside lunch at Solar dos Presuntos or a premium seafood lunch at Restaurante Feitoria (inside the Altis Belém Hotel), overlooking the Tagus — celebrated for its contemporary Portuguese cuisine.
meals.dinner: Dinner at A Cevicheria or Tasca do Chico in Príncipe Real — intimate, high-quality restaurants showcasing modern Portuguese flavors with seasonal menus and exceptional natural wine lists.

day_by_day.notes: LX Factory's Sunday market runs from approximately 10:00–18:00 and is busiest midday. Jerónimos Monastery is closed on Mondays, so Sunday is ideal. Pre-purchase Belém monument tickets online to skip queues. The Pastéis de Belém bakery can have long lines — arrive just before or after peak hours.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided deep-dive into Lisbon's history: Explore the Museu Nacional do Azulejo (National Tile Museum), housed in a stunning 16th-century convent. Discover the evolution of Portugal's iconic hand-painted azulejo tiles from Moorish origins to Baroque masterpieces — a profound window into the country's artistic and cultural identity.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Alfama district at a leisurely pace — visit the Lisbon Cathedral (Sé de Lisboa), the oldest church in the city dating to 1147, and the National Pantheon (Santa Engrácia Church) where Portugal's greatest historical figures rest. Ride the iconic Eléctrico 28 tram through the neighborhood's narrow, winding streets for an authentic local experience.
day_by_day.evening: Private sunset cruise on the Tagus River aboard a luxury sailboat or classic wooden vessel. Enjoy champagne and Portuguese canapés as the sun sets over the Belém monuments and the 25 de Abril Bridge. Return to shore for a sophisticated late dinner.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel followed by a coffee and pastel de nata at a neighborhood café — try Confeitaria Nacional near Rossio Square, one of Lisbon's oldest pastry shops.
meals.lunch: Lunch at Zé da Mouraria or Taberna da Rua das Flores — traditional Portuguese tascas (taverns) serving honest, deeply flavorful regional dishes such as migas, roast suckling pig, and clams with coriander.
meals.dinner: Post-cruise dinner at Alma (Chef Henrique Sá Pessoa, one Michelin star) in Chiado — a sophisticated celebration of Portuguese culinary heritage with an outstanding wine cellar featuring rare Douro and Alentejo labels.

day_by_day.notes: Book the private Tagus River sunset cruise at least 2–3 days in advance through a premium operator. The Tile Museum is a hidden gem — allocate at least 2 hours. Tram 28 is popular with tourists; consider riding early afternoon to avoid the busiest period.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Sintra: Board a private chauffeured car to the UNESCO-listed town of Sintra, just 40 minutes from Lisbon. Visit the fairy-tale Palácio Nacional da Pena perched dramatically above the clouds, and stroll through the lush forested grounds. Explore the romantic ruins of the Moorish Castle for sweeping views over the Atlantic coastline.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue in Sintra with a visit to the opulent Palácio Nacional de Sintra in the town center, then browse the charming village streets for local sweets such as travesseiros and queijadas. Return to Lisbon by late afternoon for final leisure time — consider a spa treatment at the hotel or last-minute shopping in Chiado for fine Portuguese products: ceramics, cork goods, and Vinho Verde.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner celebrating the end of a remarkable Lisbon journey — a grand, unhurried meal at one of Lisbon's finest tables.

meals.breakfast: Early, hearty breakfast at the hotel before departure to Sintra — fuel up with eggs, local charcuterie, and strong Portuguese coffee.
meals.lunch: Lunch in Sintra at Incomum by Luis Santos or Tascantiga — refined regional cuisine in a charming setting using fresh Serra de Sintra produce, paired with local wines.
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at Eleven Restaurant (one Michelin star) in Marquês de Pombal, offering contemporary European-Portuguese cuisine with panoramic views over Parque Eduardo VII and the city skyline — a perfect, memorable final evening in Lisbon.

day_by_day.notes: Sintra can be very busy in May — start early (depart by 9:00) to enjoy the palaces before tour groups arrive. A private driver for the Sintra day trip is highly recommended for flexibility and comfort. If departing Lisbon on May 20th, confirm hotel checkout time and arrange luggage storage or late checkout in advance.
